basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 9.' and it opens '(Cap. XLV.—Vers. 9 et 10.) Descende ergo ad me, ne steteris, et habitabis in terra Gesen'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLV.—Vers. 9 et 10.) Descende ergo ad me, ne steteris, et habitabis in terra Gesen Arabiae. Hic Arabiae additum est: in Hebraeis enim voluminibus non habetur. Unde et error increbuit, quod terra Gesen in Arabia sit. Porro si, ut in nostris codicibus est, per extremum m scribitur GESEM (גשם), quod mihi nequaquam placet, terram signat complutam; GESEM enim in imbrem vertitur.
